facts.text: Soil Sampler Arm was deployed at Chryse Planitia during Viking 1 in 1976.

The Viking lander's robotic arm could extend 3 metres to collect soil samples. It scooped Martian regolith and delivered it to three biology experiments designed to detect signs of life. The results were controversial — the Labeled Release experiment gave positive results, but scientists ultimately attributed them to chemical reactions in the soil.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Collected soil samples for three biology experiments, including the Labeled Release test that produced still-debated positive results for metabolic activity.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Chryse Planitia.
The arm rests in its final position after its last scoop; the experiment results still fuel scientific debate decades later.
